title: Four-test intervals with state and year clustering included zero in four US bird samples in 1995-2024
abstract: We tested whether uncertainty for a published ozone by seasonal warmth slope changes when errors can be related across states in the same year. We reused four fixed bird-richness model designs from the US East and West in 1995-2009 and 2010-2024. State plus year cluster intervals, adjusted for four tests, included zero in all four samples. The early western interval had narrowly excluded zero with state clustering alone. Two-way standard errors increased in two samples and decreased in two samples. All point estimates stayed fixed. We also refit each model after each year removal. This is an uncertainty audit of shared observations, not an independent biological replication. Few years, concentrated western information, selected exposure coverage, coarse weather and detection bias limit inference. The result does not prove a zero ecological effect. Code, aggregate results, source hashes, a figure and reproduction instructions are included. External survey records and model matrices remain outside the package.

display.caption: Left: intervals adjusted for four tests under three error-dependence choices. Right: estimates after each year removal. Diamonds use all years. Units are recorded species per 10 ppb ozone and 2 C warmth. These are model associations, not causal effects.

citations.reason: Exact fixed model designs, year labels and projection code. This audit changes uncertainty assumptions and removes years. Biological observations overlap.
State information concentration motivates caution about the early western signal. The current audit tests shared annual dependence.
